prompt: An alcohol is protected as R-OTMS (via TMSCl / Et₃N). Which reagent removes the TMS group to give back R-OH?

options.label: TBAF (tetrabutylammonium fluoride) — F⁻ cleaves the strong Si-O bond selectively
LiAlH₄ — hydride reduces the Si-O bond, releasing the alcohol and silane
PCC — oxidizes the silyl ether back to the alcohol
NaBH₄ — reduces the TMS group to a silane, freeing the alcohol

explanation: F⁻ has an enormous affinity for Si (Si-F ≈ 135 kcal/mol, among the strongest single bonds). TBAF cleaves silyl ethers under mild, orthogonal conditions. TMS specifically is also sensitive to water/acid. LAH and reducing agents don't selectively cleave Si-O; PCC oxidizes alcohols, not silyl ethers.
